title: Hebrews Chapter 13 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Hebrews chapter 13 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Hebrews Chapter 13 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Hebrews Chapter 13.

questions.question: In Hebrews 13, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever
Remember them which have the rule over you
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:1 states 'Let brotherly love continue' as the opening instruction of the chapter.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 13:2, what have some entertained unawares?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:2 says, 'Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.'

questions.question: What does Hebrews 13:3 instruct believers to remember?
options: Them that are in bonds and them which suffer adversity
questions.correctAnswer: Them that are in bonds and them which suffer adversity
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:3 states, 'Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them; and them which suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body.'

questions.question: According to Hebrews 13:4, what is said about marriage?
options: Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled
Marriage is a burden to bear
Marriage is only for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:4 states, 'Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled.'

questions.question: What does Hebrews 13:4 say God will judge?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:4 says, 'but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.'

questions.question: Hebrews 13:5 advises believers to have conversation without what?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:5 says, 'Let your conversation be without covetousness.'

questions.question: What promise is quoted in Hebrews 13:5 about God's presence?
options: "I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee."
"I will grant thee riches and honor."
questions.correctAnswer: "I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee."
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:5 quotes God saying, 'I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.'

questions.question: According to Hebrews 13:6, what can we boldly say about the Lord?
options: "The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me."
questions.correctAnswer: "The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me."
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:6 states, 'So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me.'

questions.question: Hebrews 13:7 instructs believers to remember whom?
options: Them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God
questions.correctAnswer: Them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:7 says, 'Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God.'

questions.question: Who is described as the same yesterday, today, and forever in Hebrews 13:8?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:8 states, 'Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.'

questions.question: Hebrews 13:9 warns against being carried about with what?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:9 says, 'Be not carried about with divers and strange doctrines.'

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 13:1 commands believers to let brotherly love continue.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:1 clearly states, 'Let brotherly love continue.'

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 13:6 says that we can boldly say, 'The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me.'
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:6 states exactly, 'So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me.'

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 13 says that believers should seek riches and honor above all else.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:5 instructs to be content with such things as you have and not be covetous, contradicting the idea of seeking riches and honor above all else.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 13 states that Jesus Christ is different from yesterday and today.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:8 says, 'Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever,' indicating no change.

medium.title: Hebrews Chapter 13 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Hebrews Chapter 13 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What do we have according to Hebrews 13:10?
questions.explanation: We have an altar, whereof they have no right to eat which serve the tabernacle. (Hebrews 13:10)

questions.question: What does Hebrews 13:12 indicate will happen to those sanctified by Jesus' blood?
options: They will suffer without the gate
questions.correctAnswer: They will suffer without the gate
questions.explanation: Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate. (Hebrews 13:12)

questions.question: According to Hebrews 13:13, what are Christians encouraged to do?
options: Go forth unto Him without the camp
questions.correctAnswer: Go forth unto Him without the camp
questions.explanation: Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach. (Hebrews 13:13)

questions.question: What does Hebrews 13:14 remind us about our current city?
options: It is a city of refuge
questions.explanation: For here have we no continuing city, but we seek one to come. (Hebrews 13:14)

questions.question: What is the sacrifice of praise mentioned in Hebrews 13:15?
options: The fruit of our lips giving thanks
questions.correctAnswer: The fruit of our lips giving thanks
questions.explanation: By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name. (Hebrews 13:15)

questions.question: According to Hebrews 13:16, what is pleasing to God?
questions.explanation: But to do good and to communicate forget not: for with such sacrifices God is well pleased. (Hebrews 13:16)

questions.question: What should believers do regarding their leaders according to Hebrews 13:17?
questions.explanation: Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls. (Hebrews 13:17)

questions.question: What does Hebrews 13:18 ask of the believers?
questions.explanation: Pray for us: for we trust we have a good conscience, in all things willing to live honestly. (Hebrews 13:18)

questions.question: What does Hebrews 13:1 encourage among believers?
questions.explanation: Let brotherly love continue. (Hebrews 13:1)

questions.question: According to Hebrews 13:3, who should we remember?
questions.explanation: Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them; and them which suffer adversity. (Hebrews 13:3)

questions.question: What is stated in Hebrews 13:5 about God's presence?
options: He will only be with the righteous
questions.explanation: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee. (Hebrews 13:5)

questions.question: What does Hebrews 13:6 enable believers to say?
options: I will fear what man can do
questions.explanation: So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me. (Hebrews 13:6)

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever according to Hebrews 13:8?
questions.explanation: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever. (Hebrews 13:8)

questions.question: Is it true that we should be carried about with divers and strange doctrines according to Hebrews 13:9?
questions.explanation: Be not carried about with divers and strange doctrines. (Hebrews 13:9)

questions.question: Is it true that God is well pleased with sacrifices of praise according to Hebrews 13:16?
questions.explanation: For with such sacrifices God is well pleased. (Hebrews 13:16) - it is the good and communication that please Him, not just any sacrifice.

hard.title: Hebrews Chapter 13 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Hebrews Chapter 13.

questions.question: What does the author beseech the readers to do in Hebrews 13:19?
questions.explanation: The author beseeches the readers to do this so he may be restored to them sooner, as stated in Hebrews 13:19.

questions.question: Who is referred to as 'the great shepherd of the sheep' in Hebrews 13:20?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:20 refers to Jesus as 'the great shepherd of the sheep.'

questions.question: What does Hebrews 13:21 say God will make perfect in believers?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:21 states that God will make you perfect in every good work to do His will.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the letter mentioned in Hebrews 13:22?
questions.explanation: The author writes that he has written a letter in few words to exhort the brethren, as stated in Hebrews 13:22.

questions.question: What does the author ask for in Hebrews 13:18?
questions.explanation: In Hebrews 13:18, the author requests the readers to pray for them.

questions.question: In Hebrews 13:24, whom does the author ask the readers to salute?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:24 instructs to salute all them that have rule over them and all the saints.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'teleioo' in Hebrews 13:21 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Teleioo' means 'to complete' or 'to make perfect,' which aligns with the context in Hebrews 13:21.

questions.question: What literary device is used in the phrase 'the God of peace' in Hebrews 13:20?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'the God of peace' is an epithet, describing God with a specific characteristic in Hebrews 13:20.

questions.question: Which passage reflects the theme of brotherly love found in Hebrews 13:1?
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:7 reflects the theme of brotherly love, stating, 'Beloved, let us love one another.'

questions.question: Which Old Testament verse highlights God's everlasting covenant as mentioned in Hebrews 13:20?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:33 speaks of God's covenant with Israel, which is echoed in Hebrews 13:20 regarding the everlasting covenant.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Hebrews 13:19?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:19 follows directly after Hebrews 13:18, which requests prayer for the author.

questions.question: What comes after Hebrews 13:21?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:22 follows Hebrews 13:21, where the author continues exhorting the brethren.

questions.question: The phrase 'to communicate forget not' in Hebrews 13:16 suggests what cultural practice?
questions.explanation: The phrase in Hebrews 13:16 emphasizes the cultural importance of hospitality and sharing with others.

questions.question: The statement 'Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever' in Hebrews 13:8 is what?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:8 affirms the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ.

questions.question: The author of Hebrews is accused of having written a long letter in Hebrews 13:22.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:22 states that the author has written a letter in few words, not a long one.

theological.title: Hebrews Chapter 13 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Hebrews Chapter 13 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 13:1 teach about Christian relationships?
options: The doctrine of continuing brotherly love as a fundamental Christian ethic
The doctrine of ritual purity in communal worship
The doctrine of predestination regarding the elect
The doctrine of justification by faith alone
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of continuing brotherly love as a fundamental Christian ethic
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:1 exhorts believers to let brotherly love continue, teaching the doctrine that love among Christians is ongoing and essential.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 13:8 teach about the person of Christ?
options: The doctrine of Christ’s immutability and eternal constancy
The doctrine of Christ’s subordination to angels
The doctrine of Christ’s temporary earthly ministry only
The doctrine of Christ’s changing nature according to the age
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of Christ’s immutability and eternal constancy
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:8 states that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, affirming His divine immutability.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning salvation is taught in Hebrews 13:12?
options: The doctrine of Jesus’ atoning sacrifice outside the camp for sanctification
The doctrine of salvation by works through the Law
The doctrine of universal salvation without judgment
The doctrine of Jesus’ physical resurrection as a mere miracle
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of Jesus’ atoning sacrifice outside the camp for sanctification
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:12 explains that Jesus suffered outside the gate to sanctify people by His own blood, teaching substitutionary atonement.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 13:5 specifically demonstrate?
options: God’s covenant faithfulness to never leave or forsake His people
God’s omniscience in knowing all desires of the heart
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant faithfulness to never leave or forsake His people
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:5 quotes God’s promise, 'I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee,' demonstrating His covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 13:20 demonstrate?
options: God’s power over death in raising Jesus the great shepherd
questions.correctAnswer: God’s power over death in raising Jesus the great shepherd
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:20 speaks of God who brought back from the dead our Lord Jesus, showing His sovereign power over death.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 13:3 prepare for the New Testament theme of corporate solidarity in suffering?
options: By teaching believers to remember those in prison and suffering as if they themselves are suffering
By emphasizing individual salvation apart from community
By discouraging involvement in social justice
By teaching that suffering is only for unbelievers
questions.correctAnswer: By teaching believers to remember those in prison and suffering as if they themselves are suffering
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:3 calls believers to remember those in bonds and adversity as if sharing their suffering, anticipating the New Testament theme of communal solidarity.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 13:14 connect to the eschatological hope revealed throughout Scripture?
options: It teaches that believers seek a heavenly city, reflecting the biblical promise of a new heaven and earth
It teaches that earthly cities are eternal and ultimate
It denies any future hope beyond this life
It teaches reincarnation into earthly cities
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that believers seek a heavenly city, reflecting the biblical promise of a new heaven and earth
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:14 states that we have no continuing city here but seek one to come, echoing Scripture’s eschatological hope of a heavenly city (cf. Revelation 21).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 13:15 and 13:16 teach about Christian worship and ethics?
options: Worship includes continual praise and ethical action, both pleasing to God
Worship is only ritual without ethical demands
Ethics are separate from worship and irrelevant
Praise is optional and unrelated to doing good
questions.correctAnswer: Worship includes continual praise and ethical action, both pleasing to God
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:15 commands continual praise, and 13:16 commands to do good and share, teaching worship is both verbal praise and ethical deeds.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 13:10 and 13:11 teach about the relationship between the old covenant sacrifices and Christ’s priesthood?
options: The old sacrifices were external and temporary, but Christ’s altar is eternal and exclusive
The old sacrifices remain valid alongside Christ’s priesthood
Christ’s priesthood is subordinate to the tabernacle sacrifices
The old sacrifices were more effective than Christ’s sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: The old sacrifices were external and temporary, but Christ’s altar is eternal and exclusive
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:10-11 contrasts the temporary tabernacle sacrifices with the true altar Christians have in Christ, whose priesthood surpasses the old.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 13:6 and 13:17 teach about Christian confidence and submission to leaders?
options: Believers have bold confidence in God’s help and are called to obediently submit to spiritual leaders
Believers should fear leaders more than God
Submission to leaders is optional and independent of faith
Confidence in God excludes any human authority
questions.correctAnswer: Believers have bold confidence in God’s help and are called to obediently submit to spiritual leaders
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:6 affirms confidence in the Lord as helper, and 13:17 commands obedience to leaders who watch over souls, linking trust in God with submission.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Hebrews 13:9 teaches legalism by forbidding all new teachings. What does Hebrews 13:9 actually teach?
options: It warns against being carried about by strange doctrines emphasizing external rituals over grace
It commands strict adherence to dietary laws
It forbids all forms of doctrinal development
It promotes legalistic observance of meats for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: It warns against being carried about by strange doctrines emphasizing external rituals over grace
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:9 cautions against strange doctrines and teaches the heart should be established with grace, not external observances like meats.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 13:4 teach about marriage and sexual ethics?
options: Marriage is honorable and the marital bed undefiled; God judges immoral sexual behavior
Marriage is irrelevant to Christian life
Sexual immorality is not subject to divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Marriage is honorable and the marital bed undefiled; God judges immoral sexual behavior
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:4 affirms the honor of marriage and warns that whoremongers and adulterers face God’s judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 13:21 specifically demonstrate?
options: God’s sanctifying power working in believers to do His will
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sanctifying power working in believers to do His will
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:21 prays for God to perfect believers in every good work, working in them what is pleasing, demonstrating God’s sanctifying power.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 13:7 and 13:24 teach about spiritual leadership and fellowship?
options: Believers are to remember and imitate faithful leaders and greet fellow saints in unity
Leaders are to be ignored and saints isolated
Spiritual leadership is irrelevant to Christian growth
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are to remember and imitate faithful leaders and greet fellow saints in unity
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:7 calls remembering leaders who spoke God’s word and imitating their faith, 13:24 sends greetings to leaders and saints, emphasizing unity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 13:2 teach about hospitality and divine encounter?
options: Some who entertain strangers may unknowingly entertain angels, teaching the sacredness of hospitality
Hospitality is unnecessary and unrelated to faith
Hospitality is only a cultural custom without spiritual significance
questions.correctAnswer: Some who entertain strangers may unknowingly entertain angels, teaching the sacredness of hospitality
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:2 warns not to forget hospitality, for some have entertained angels unawares, teaching its spiritual importance.
